title: Sentence Improvement
tagline: Year 2 — Replacing a faulty part of a sentence with the best alternative

introduction.overview: In a sentence-improvement question, part of the sentence is marked and four alternatives are offered: usually one of them repeats the original ("No improvement") and the others are possible replacements. You choose the version that makes the sentence grammatically correct, clear and natural. The skill is similar to error detection, but you must also choose the right correction among close alternatives.
introduction.placementRelevance: Sentence improvement questions are commonly asked in the verbal ability section of company aptitude rounds, along with error detection and sentence completion.
introduction.realWorldContext: Editing a draft, rewriting a clumsy sentence and polishing an email use the same judgement.

learningObjectives: Identify the error type in the marked part
Choose the correction that fits the rest of the sentence
Recognise when the sentence is already correct
Keep the meaning unchanged while correcting the grammar

prerequisiteKnowledge.quickRefresher: Use the same checklist as in error detection: agreement, tense and verb form, preposition, article, pronoun, comparison, conjunction.

coreDefinitions: Underlined (bracketed) part: the portion that may be replaced.
No improvement: the option that repeats the original part; correct if the sentence is already right.
Meaning-preserving correction: the replacement must keep the original meaning.
Parallel structure: items in a list or comparison should have the same grammatical form.
Redundancy: needless words that repeat an idea.
conceptExplanation.theoreticalIntuition: Read the whole sentence first, then read it again with each alternative in place of the bracketed part. The best alternative gives a correct sentence with the same meaning. If the original reads correctly, "No improvement" is the answer.
conceptExplanation.visualOrMentalModel: Identify the error type from the bracketed part, think of the correct form, and then look for it among the options. Eliminate options that introduce a new error.

importantRulesAndFormulas.title: Agreement
importantRulesAndFormulas.formula: Subject and verb must match in number
importantRulesAndFormulas.simpleExample: The cost of the repairs has increased

importantRulesAndFormulas.title: Verb form
importantRulesAndFormulas.formula: did + V1; had + V3; to + V1 / -ing after a preposition

importantRulesAndFormulas.title: Fixed pairs
importantRulesAndFormulas.formula: prefer to; good at; senior to; look forward to + -ing

importantRulesAndFormulas.title: Comparison
importantRulesAndFormulas.formula: Comparative for two, superlative for three or more
importantRulesAndFormulas.description: Better of two, best of three.

importantRulesAndFormulas.title: Conjunction patterns
importantRulesAndFormulas.formula: No sooner … than; hardly … when; the reason is that
importantRulesAndFormulas.simpleExample: No sooner had she left than it rained

mainNarrative: Work out what is wrong with the bracketed part. In "She [don't like] tea", the subject she needs doesn't. In "They [was playing] football", the plural subject needs were playing.
Check fixed expressions. "I look forward [to meet] you" needs to meeting you. "She is good [in] maths" needs at. "The reason is [because] he was late" needs that.
Check comparisons. "He is the best of the two" should be "the better of the two", since a comparison of two takes the comparative. Double comparatives such as more taller are wrong.
Check conjunction patterns. "No sooner had she left [when] it rained" needs than; "Hardly had he reached [than] the train left" needs when.
If the part is already correct, select "No improvement". When two options look correct, choose the one that keeps the original meaning and the simplest grammar.

deepDiveAspects.title: Do not over-correct
deepDiveAspects.content: Some alternatives change the meaning or are stylistically heavier. Choose the minimal correction that fixes the error.

deepDiveAspects.title: Check the full sentence
deepDiveAspects.content: A replacement may fix the marked part but clash with another word. Always read the full sentence with your choice.

solvedExamples.title: Verb form
solvedExamples.question: He [did not came] yesterday.
solvedExamples.conceptOrFormula: After did not, use the base form.

steps.title: Spot
steps.explanation: "Did not" already carries the past tense.

solvedExamples.title: Comparison
solvedExamples.question: He is [the best of the two] brothers.
givenInfo: Bracketed: the best of the two
solvedExamples.whyItWorks: The superlative is for three or more.

solvedExamples.title: Conjunction pair
solvedExamples.question: No sooner had she left [when] it rained.
solvedExamples.whyItWorks: Hardly takes when, no sooner takes than.

traditionalVsShortcut.traditionalMethod: Try each option in the sentence.
traditionalVsShortcut.shortcutMethod: Name the error type, form the correct word yourself, and then find it among the options.

placementTips.eliminationTechnique: Eliminate options that repeat the error.
placementTips.questionSelectionAdvice: Name the error before looking at options.
placementTips.recruiterInsight: Close options usually differ in one word.

quickFormulas: better of two, best of three
